industry.fy27View: HMIL MD (30-Jul-2026): industry growth strong in H1 on the low pre-GST base, 'lower single digits' in H2, 6-9% for FY27.
industry.westAsia: US-Iran conflict from the end of FY26 disrupted shipping to the Middle East (Strait of Hormuz); HMIL redirected exports to Central and South America (+23% in Q1FY27) and Mexico (q1call).
industry.rupee: INR 95.7 per US$ on 30-Jul-2026 (JM Financial): helps export realisations, raises the cost of imported parts and the royalty paid to HMC.
industry.cafe: CAFE-II (FY23-27): HMIL expects no penalty under the revised draft; CAFE-III draft rules out for consultation (q1call, q4call).

excluded.BAJAJ-AUTO: Earnings distorted: the Mar-2026 quarter carries ~Rs1,894 cr of other income when Bajaj took control of KTM, and KTM is consolidated from that quarter, so its trailing P/E on 30-Sep-2026 sits on an inflated TTM EPS (same treatment as in our Eicher report).
excluded.ESCORTS: Earnings distorted: a Rs1,085 cr exceptional gain on selling the railway-equipment business (Jun-2025 quarter) depressed its trailing P/E series, and the company that remains is not the one in its history (same treatment as in our Eicher report).

governance.relatedParty: HMC (82.5%) is also the technology licensor and a supplier. Royalty to HMC Rs1,975 cr in FY26 (2.8% of revenue; Rs1,878 cr in FY25); ~30% of FY26 purchases (Rs15,700 cr of Rs53,072 cr) came from group companies (Mobis India Rs8,733 cr, Hyundai Transys Lear Rs1,943 cr, Kia India Rs1,736 cr, HMC Rs1,479 cr, Hyundai's Indonesian plant Rs1,085 cr); HMIL sold Rs2,347 cr to Kia India and Rs1,731 cr to Hyundai Mexico. In Mar-2025 shareholders voted on seven related-party resolutions worth ~Rs31,526 cr (~40% of revenue); proxy adviser SES recommended voting against six, IiAS supported all.
governance.capitalAllocation: Paid ~Rs15,400 cr of dividends to HMC in FY24 before the IPO (derived from the fall in reserves); the IPO was a pure sale by HMC (Rs27,859 cr), so none of the money came to the company. Since listing: Rs21 a share each year (~30-31% payout) while capex steps up to Rs7,500 cr (FY27) as part of a Rs45,000 cr FY26-30 plan.
governance.auditor: BSR & Co. LLP (KPMG network); unqualified opinion

moat: Brands and products
Moderate
Creta has ~30% of India's mid-SUV segment (AR FY26) and is the group's anchor; Venue, Exter, i20 and Verna fill the range; SUVs 68-70% of domestic volume
Pricing power is real in Creta but not across the range: Hyundai lost share in compact SUVs and hatchbacks to M&M, Tata and Maruti
Parent's technology
Strong (but rented)

Platforms, engines, EV and hybrid know-how from HMC (Hyundai Motor Group is the world's third-largest carmaker by passenger-vehicle sales, per the company); Rs1,975 cr royalty in FY26 (2.8% of revenue)
Access to world-class technology without the R&D bill, at the cost of a permanent royalty and dependence on the parent's product decisions
Scale and cost
Moderate
994k capacity (Chennai 824k + Pune 170k), localisation 83% (target 90% by 2030), EBITDA margin 12-13% vs Maruti's 11-12% (FY26)
Good cost position, but Maruti is 3x its size and M&M earns higher margins in SUVs
Export hub
Strong
India's largest cumulative PV exporter; 190,125 vehicles exported in FY26 (+16.4%); HMC sources the new Venue from India; export revenue 25.6% of FY26
A second engine of growth that Indian rivals lack; exposed to the Middle East and to currency swings
Distribution and service
Moderate
1,519 sales and 1,679 service outlets (Jun-2026); 6 of 10 new outlets rural; rural share 25.9%
Wide, but not unique: Maruti's network is far larger
Electrification
Weak so far
Hyundai's EV range in India is small today (Creta Electric); the first localised mass-market EV arrives in H2FY27; Tata and M&M lead EVs
An option, not yet an advantage
critiques: Hyundai has lost domestic share for three years (14.6% in FY24, 12.6% in FY26) and slipped from #2 to #4 behind M&M and Tata; one launch a year is not enough in an SUV market where rivals launch several
Autocar Pro (1-Apr-2026); Morgan Stanley (Sep-2026: share near its low)
Exports depend heavily on the Middle East; the West Asia conflict cut Q1 exports 20% and August 31%: 'we remain cautious on the export outlook'
Margins are volatile and under pressure from commodities (precious metals, copper), Pune ramp-up costs and the growth push
JM Financial, BOB Caps, Morgan Stanley (Apr-2026 target cut on cost pressure)
The parent extracts value through royalty and parts purchases; the related-party approvals sought in 2025 equalled ~40% of revenue
SES (proxy adviser) via Business Standard, Mar-2025

GAM Research; brokers' FY27E EPS of Rs67-69 imply ~flat earnings
